mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, which raises discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in >60% of instances despite FEDFUNDS rising by >1% over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC >0.05 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate below 7.5% triggers a labor market adjustment, reducing growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 7.5% in the current month
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive when UNRATE crosses below 7.5% but remains above for 3 months, or IC rank exceeds 0.05 over a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices signals a balanced economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and INDPRO increase in the same month
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative despite both GDPC1 and INDPRO rising by >2% in the same month, or IC rank <0.03 over a 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, sustained low federal funds rates below 2% signal accommodative monetary policy, compressing discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative when FEDFUNDS remain below 2% but the IC rank exceeds 0.05 over a 9-month window, or returns are not significantly higher than baseline (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High labor participation rates (PAYEMS) indicate strong job market activity, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative despite PAYEMS rising by >5% month-over-month, or IC rank <0.03 over a 2-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in quarterly demand (GDPC1) exceeding 5% from the prior quarter signals robust economic growth, prompting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 exceeds prior quarter's value by >5%
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 exceeds the threshold by >5%, or IC rank <0.03 over a 3-quarter window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) coupled with rising demand (GDPC1) creates a favorable environment for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases while GDPC1 increases in the same month
regime_hint: monetary easing combined with demand growth
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative despite FEDFUNDS falling and GDPC1 rising by >3% in the same month, or IC rank <0.03 over a 1-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the supply index (INDPRO) below 95 signals a potential supply shock, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive when INDPRO drops below 95 but recovers within 3 months, or IC rank exceeds 0.05 over a 4-month window.
